newsitem.title: USA: Offshore Energy Viosca well producing.
newsitem.headline: Offshore Energy Viosca well producing.

text.p: Offshore Energy Development Corp said Tuesday its Viosca Knoll 35 No. 1 well is flowing at a rate of 3.3 million cubic feet of natural gas per day.

The company said this 1,296-foot deep well is located offshore Alabama in the Gulf of Mexico. Owned 100 percent by Offshore Energy, Viosca Knoll 35 is being produced through Enron Oil & Gas Co's platform and facilities located in Viosca Knoll 124.
The company also said the Viosca Knoll 122 A-1 sidetrack that was started in July has been completed and flow tested at a rate of 2.0 million cubic feet per day.
The drilling rig has been moved to Viosca Knoll 123, where sidetrack operations will start.

Viosca Knoll blocks 122 and 123 are owned by a partnership between Offshore Energy and Joint Energy Development Investments LP, an investment affiliate of Enron Corp. Offshore Energy's interest in the partnership, South Dauphin Partners II LP, is currently 25 percent.

The company also said it recently expanded its banking facility with Union Bank of California. The borrowing base under the new agreement increases to $11 million from under $3 million. The borrowing base is subject to quarterly adjustment.
Offshore Energy said it anticipates this new facility will be fully used in 1997 to pursue additional exploration and production activities.

The company said the recent successful public offering of shares in an Asian Pacific oil refining project, InterOil Corp, resulted in Offshore Energy's minority interest being valued at more than $4.3 million. Its basis in this 1995 investment is $250,000.
The company said it has no plans to liquidate its holdings in the project.
